questions.q: In Azure's resource model, what does a virtual machine attach to, and what does that attach to in turn?
options: An availability zone, which attaches to a VNet
A resource group, which attaches to a subnet
A subnet directly, with no intermediate resource
A network interface, which attaches to a subnet
questions.explain: Azure VMs never attach to a subnet directly — they attach to a network interface (azurerm_network_interface), and the NIC's ip_configuration block attaches to the subnet.

questions.q: Why is network_interface_ids on azurerm_linux_virtual_machine a list, even in this lesson's single-NIC example?
options: Because an Azure VM can have more than one network interface attached
Because Azure VMs always have exactly two NICs by default
Because it actually holds subnet IDs, not NIC IDs
Because Terraform requires every argument to be a list
questions.explain: The schema is a list because Azure allows a VM to have multiple NICs, even though a single-NIC VM like this lesson's only needs one entry in it.

questions.q: How does aws_instance attach to a subnet, compared to how azurerm_linux_virtual_machine does?
options: aws_instance cannot be placed into a subnet at all
aws_instance references the subnet directly via subnet_id — no separate network-interface resource is required
aws_instance uses availability_zone instead of subnet_id
aws_instance also requires a separate aws_network_interface resource in every configuration
questions.explain: aws_instance sets subnet_id = aws_subnet.web.id directly. AWS creates an elastic network interface (ENI) behind the scenes automatically, without requiring an explicit resource for the common single-NIC case.

questions.q: What does source_image_reference do on azurerm_linux_virtual_machine, and what is its rough AWS equivalent on aws_instance?
options: It names the resource group; tags is the equivalent
It specifies which marketplace image to boot from; ami plays the equivalent role on aws_instance
It sets the VM's size; instance_type is the equivalent
It configures the private IP address; it has no AWS equivalent
questions.explain: source_image_reference identifies the OS image (publisher, offer, sku, version) to boot from on Azure; ami does the same job by referencing a machine image ID on AWS.

questions.q: Why does AWS not require a separate network-interface resource for a basic aws_instance, while Azure requires azurerm_network_interface?
options: AWS creates an elastic network interface (ENI) implicitly behind aws_instance, while Azure treats the NIC as a first-class, independently manageable resource
AWS requires an explicit NIC resource too, just with a different name
Azure's network interface resource is optional and was only included for demonstration
AWS instances don't actually have network interfaces at all
questions.explain: Azure models the NIC as its own detachable, reusable resource. AWS creates an ENI automatically behind aws_instance, and you'd only manage one explicitly if a VM needed more than its default single NIC.
